clue.text: Game for an old school get-together

parts.note: Rugby School, the old public school in Warwickshire where the game is said to have begun
a union is a coming together or joining

explanation.surface: Someone picks a match to play at an old boys' reunion.
explanation.walkthrough: Rugby is a famous English private school, which gave its name to the sport.
explanation.definitionFit: Rugby union is the fifteen-a-side form of the football code, a sport.

clue.text: Tree Father planted in N America

indicators.note: put into the ground inside, so one piece is set within the other

parts.note: the US is in North America
pa is an informal word for father

explanation.surface: Dad has put a tree in the ground in North America.
explanation.walkthrough: The upas is a Javanese tree whose sap is poisonous.
explanation.definitionFit: The upas is a poisonous tropical tree of south-east Asia.

clue.text: Wine container under the counter

indicators.note: in a down clue the second piece sits beneath the first

parts.note: a bar is a counter where drinks are served
a sac is a bag-like container in biology

explanation.surface: A bottle of wine is kept stashed below the bar.
explanation.definitionFit: Barsac is a sweet white Bordeaux from the commune of that name.

clue.text: Old city features ragged children

parts.note: Ur was an ancient city of Mesopotamia
chins are facial features

explanation.surface: An ancient city is home to poor scruffy kids.
explanation.definitionFit: Street urchins are poor, scruffy youngsters.

clue.text: I have an old-fashioned image

parts.note: I'd is the short form of I had, I have
ol' is a folksy, dated spelling of old

explanation.surface: Someone confesses to owning a dated picture.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'an' is a link word; OL' is the dialect form of old.
explanation.definitionFit: An idol is a carved or graven image worshipped as a god.

clue.text: It joins another for a breather

definitions.text: It joins another for a breather

parts.words: It joins another for a breather
parts.note: a breather is not a rest but something to breathe through, working as one of a pair

explanation.definitionFit: Each opening of the nose works with its twin to let air in.

clue.text: Two features of wild scenery portrayed in "Wuthering Heights"

parts.note: a heath is open moorland
a cliff is a steep rock face

explanation.surface: Moorland and crags are depicted in the Brontë novel.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a character portrayed in Emily Brontë's novel, its brooding hero.
explanation.definitionFit: He is the brooding, vengeful hero of Emily Brontë's novel.

clue.text: Lacking resolve, Tories rule badly

indicators.note: done badly, the letters are put in the wrong order

explanation.surface: A jibe that the Conservatives govern poorly and indecisively.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone hesitant and unable to decide is wavering.

clue.text: Double this for agreement, understand!

explanation.surface: A shout of approval, doubled, and a plea to grasp something.
explanation.walkthrough: In Parliament members say the word twice over to show they agree with a speaker.
explanation.definitionFit: Repeated, it is the British parliamentary cry of approval; alone it means to take in or grasp what is said.

clue.text: Island with many debts is undependable

parts.note: Capri is an island in the Bay of Naples
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, so a large number
IOUs are written promises to pay, so debts

explanation.surface: Someone living on an island while running up debts cannot be relied on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Many' giving C uses the Roman numeral 100, a standard crossword trick.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone fickle and given to sudden whims cannot be relied upon.

clue.text: Produce nippers

parts.note: nippers looks like slang for small children, but here means teeth, which a baby grows

explanation.definitionFit: A baby cutting its first teeth is growing its biting equipment.

clue.text: A second order of clergy

parts.note: the ministers ranking just beneath priests in the church hierarchy

explanation.definitionFit: In the church these ministers rank below priests, an order of ordained assistants.

clue.text: Girl allowed her aunt in Paris to be a dabbler

parts.note: Di is a short girl's name
let means allowed
tante is French for aunt

explanation.surface: A girl is permitted to have her French aunt be an amateur.
explanation.definitionFit: A dilettante dabbles in the arts without serious commitment.

clue.text: He has lots to offer

parts.note: lots are not plenty but items numbered for sale at an auction

explanation.definitionFit: At a sale room he takes bids on each numbered item.

clue.text: Why so unusually ostentatious?

indicators.note: arranged in an unusual way, the letters come out in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone asks why a thing is so strangely flashy.
explanation.definitionFit: Something flashy and ostentatious is meant to be noticed.

clue.text: An oppressive blow for the Italians

definitions.text: An oppressive blow for the Italians

parts.words: An oppressive blow for the Italians
parts.note: a blow here is a gust of wind, a hot dusty one reaching Italy from Africa

explanation.definitionFit: It is the hot, humid Saharan wind that sweeps across the Mediterranean to southern Italy.

clue.text: In a way quite small, but totally delightful

indicators.note: one word placed inside another, put in the abbreviation

parts.note: ST, short for street, is a way
wee means small

explanation.surface: Something small in a way yet utterly charming.
explanation.definitionFit: Something sweet is charming and lovely.

clue.text: Wrap around one's shoulders

parts.note: a garment worn draped over the upper body, read as a description

explanation.definitionFit: A square or length of cloth worn over the shoulders is this kind of wrap.

clue.text: See award for natural feature of Scotland

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look or see
CH, the Companion of Honour, a British honour

explanation.surface: Someone is told to take note of a prize given for Scottish scenery.
explanation.walkthrough: CH stands for Companion of Honour, an award in the British honours system.
explanation.definitionFit: A Scottish lake or sea inlet is a common feature of that landscape.

clue.text: Use deception to get university place

parts.note: to lie is to deceive

explanation.surface: A cheat lies their way into a college place.
explanation.definitionFit: The word survives in the phrase 'in lieu of', meaning in place of.

clue.text: Very little in starting price — should clean up!

indicators.note: the small word sits inside the betting abbreviation

parts.note: SP is the betting abbreviation for starting price
wee is Scottish for small

explanation.surface: A racegoer backs a long shot at very short odds, hoping to win big.
explanation.walkthrough: SP is the bookmakers' starting price; a sweep (sweepstake) also suits the racing picture.
explanation.definitionFit: A chimney sweep or a broom is someone or something whose job is to clean up.

clue.text: RAF's set to scramble in attacks

indicators.note: scramble means mix up, and also suits the RAF picture of fighters taking off

explanation.surface: The Royal Air Force get ready to launch their fighters for raids.
explanation.walkthrough: Scramble is an RAF term for a fast take-off, but here it mixes letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To strafe is to attack with gunfire from low-flying aircraft.

clue.text: New pointer of benefit to consumers

indicators.note: made new, the letters are recast in a fresh order

explanation.surface: A fresh tip that helps shoppers.
explanation.walkthrough: Consumers here are eaters, not shoppers: the nutrient benefits those who eat it.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a nutrient that does good to those who eat it.

clue.text: Feeling like a local visit?

parts.note: a local is British slang for a nearby pub, so this is wanting a drink

explanation.walkthrough: In Britain 'the local' is one's neighbourhood pub.
explanation.definitionFit: Wanting a drink is what would send someone to the pub.

clue.text: Kind of shirt with a frill-very tasteful

parts.note: T as in a T-shirt
a ruffle is a gathered frill

explanation.surface: A fashion note on a T-shirt trimmed with a frill being in very good taste.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tasteful' here means full of flavour, not stylish: the fungus is a prized delicacy.
explanation.definitionFit: This prized underground fungus is a strongly flavoured gourmet delicacy.

clue.text: Not sound advice if this tap gets stuck!

definitions.text: Not sound advice if this tap gets stuck!

parts.words: Not sound advice if this tap gets stuck!
parts.note: the word for this tap is said like the advice to use brute strength, which is bad counsel for a stuck tap

explanation.walkthrough: The American word for a tap sounds like 'force it', poor advice when a tap jams.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the American word for a tap that controls water flow.

clue.text: It will treat bruises in a car smash

indicators.note: a car smash wrecks things, so these letters are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone bruised in a car crash will need a remedy.
explanation.definitionFit: This herbal preparation from a mountain plant is a traditional ointment for bruising.

clue.text: Big name appears nightly

explanation.surface: A celebrity performs every evening.
explanation.definitionFit: A celebrity is a famous name; a heavenly body shines in the sky after dark.

clue.text: Victoria thumbed by Jack for a lift?

definitions.text: Victoria thumbed by Jack for a lift?

parts.words: Victoria thumbed by Jack for a lift?
parts.note: Victoria is a fruit variety, and in the nursery rhyme Little Jack Horner put in his thumb and pulled one out

explanation.walkthrough: Little Jack Horner 'put in his thumb and pulled out a' fruit; 'thumbed for a lift' suggests hitchhiking at Victoria station.
explanation.definitionFit: The Victoria is a well-known variety of this stone fruit.

clue.text: The prodigal son's return fare

parts.note: fare is food, not a ticket price, served at a homecoming in the Bible parable

explanation.walkthrough: In the parable in Luke 15, the father kills a fattened animal to feast the returning son.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Gospel parable the father slaughters this beast to celebrate the son coming home.

clue.text: Aunt weeps, admits being excessively sentimental

indicators.note: the two words let the answer in, holding it inside them

explanation.surface: An aunt cries and confesses to being over-emotional.
explanation.definitionFit: Something cutesy and sugary is overly quaint or sentimental.

clue.text: The shooting season

parts.note: not the time for hunting game, but when plants put out new shoots

explanation.definitionFit: Spring is when new growth sprouts from plants.
